realizeEconomics(bytes32,(address,addres.details: Called ONLY by this contract via `this.realizeEconomics(...)`, so a revert      anywhere inside rolls back EVERY state change below — controller      obligations, cap burn, budget burn, transfers, backing decrement — while      afterSwap's try/catch absorbs it and the swap completes with zero delta.      This is the ONLY fail-open boundary; GenesisDistLib no longer catches.      CUSTODY (Model A): the FULL D leaves the hook here.        trader      -> PoolManager (settled; negative unspecified delta)        D - trader  -> controller's vault (lp+protocol+router+keeper+dust)      Backing is therefore decremented by D, not by the trader share, so no      token is ever both hook trader-backing and controller-reserved backing.

updateOracleHeartbeat((address,address,u.notice: Refresh the pool oracle using current pool price without a swap.         Keeps oracle.lastBlock current so subsequent external corrective         swaps pass the staleness gate in _isCorrectiveSwap. Security properties:   keeper-only        Prevents attacker from calling after their own                      manipulative swap to encode a distorted price.   one-per-block      At most one heartbeat per block, all pools.   spot-movement gate Refuses sqrtPriceX96 movement over 2 % from EMA.                      This is a sqrt-price bound (about 4 % in token price),                      not a general economic manipulation-proof guarantee.   same OracleLib.update as afterSwap (EMA and recent per-block samples).   sample semantics   Internal twap fields are recent samples, not a timed TWAP.                      The external v3 reader supplies the separate timed TWAP.   no economics       No corrective flag, no vault writes, no ROFR emitted.   notPaused          Disabled when hook is paused.   Gas ~45,000 vs ~200,000+ for a dust swap.
